metadata.title: Pertuzumab/Trastuzumab (Phesgo®) and Vinorelbine Therapy
metadata.indication: Treatment of adults with HER2-positive metastatic or locally recurrent unresectable breast cancer without previous anti-HER2 therapy or chemotherapy for metastatic disease, when taxane therapy is clinically unsuitable.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Source reconciled · clinical/pharmacy approval pending
encoding_maturity.scope_note: Audit of source indication, route, blood counts, organ function, cardiac/reaction criteria, source ambiguities and longitudinal checks. No independent clinical authorisation.

metadata.catalogue_source_check_scope: Catalogue presence and source link structure only; not rule level source fidelity.
audit_limitations: Vinorelbine grade ≥3 adverse-event row contains conflicting reduction/discontinuation text; source clarification and specialist review required.
NCCP gives no quantified restart row for ANC<0.5 or platelets<75; hold/review without inventing a numerical restart.
The oral Navelbine SmPC has stricter blood-count thresholds and different hepatic guidance than the unspecific NCCP table; oral rules require explicit source/product reconciliation.
The route must be confirmed before prescribing vinorelbine; IV and oral alternatives require different dose and supportive-care plans.
Oral vinorelbine is moderate–high emetic risk in NCCP V6 Table8; regimen PDF minimal label is insufficient for the oral route.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Any dose modification should be discussed with a Consultant.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding of the current NCCP source. It does not replace the NCCP regimen, clinical judgement, local policy, prescribing review or pharmacy verification.

neuropathy_grade.label: Peripheral neuropathy grade
neuropathy_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess sensory and/or motor symptoms and their effect on instrumental versus self-care activities of daily living. Distinguish transient cold sensitivity from persistent functional neuropathy.

constipation_grade.label: Constipation grade
constipation_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess change from baseline, need for laxatives, interference with activities, manual evacuation, obstruction and hospitalisation.

other_toxicity_grade.label: Other toxicity grade
other_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Identify the actual adverse event first, then apply that toxicity-specific CTCAE definition. The generic severity anchors are not a substitute for the named CTCAE criterion.

options.label: HER2-positive advanced breast cancer; no prior metastatic chemotherapy/HER2 treatment; taxane unsuitable

lvef_drop_points.label: Absolute LVEF fall from pretreatment value (percentage points)

hypersensitivity_grade.label: Infusion/hypersensitivity reaction grade
hypersensitivity_grade.assessment_guidance: Document timing, symptoms, need to interrupt treatment, response to symptomatic therapy, recurrence, hospitalisation and any airway or haemodynamic compromise.

diarrhoea_grade.label: Diarrhoea grade
diarrhoea_grade.assessment_guidance: Count stools per day above the patient's baseline, assess ostomy output, continence, hydration, fever, abdominal pain, haemodynamic compromise and whether hospital care is indicated.

diarrhoea_not_improving.label: Severe/prolonged diarrhoea not improving with supportive treatment

bronchospasm_or_ards.label: Bronchospasm or acute respiratory distress syndrome during HER2 reaction

disease_progression.label: Disease progression or loss of benefit

The NCCP grade ≥3 row states recovery to grade 1 followed by 80% of original dose, but also contains an unqualified discontinuation instruction. Do not select an automatic restart or permanent-stop pathway until the toxicity and source ambiguity are resolved.

action.recommendation: Oral vinorelbine needs its own moderate–high emetic-risk plan with an oral 5-HT3 antagonist under NCCP guidance. Do not apply the minimal-risk IV script. Confirm the D1/D8 prescription; swallow capsules whole with food, and do not repeat a dose after vomiting.

action.recommendation: The interval is at least 6 weeks: verify the actual prior doses and reloading plan for Phesgo 1200 mg/600 mg SC over 8 minutes followed by 30 minutes observation; then 600 mg/600 mg every 3 weeks. Other safety checks still apply.

rules.explanation: The interval is at least 6 weeks: verify the actual prior doses and reloading plan for Phesgo 1200 mg/600 mg SC over 8 minutes followed by 30 minutes observation; then 600 mg/600 mg every 3 weeks. Other safety checks still apply.

action.recommendation: For a gap under 6 weeks, confirm the actual previous doses and use Phesgo 600 mg/600 mg SC as soon as possible, then every 3 weeks. The same interval rule applies when switching from IV HER2 medicines. This is interval guidance, not overall clearance.

action.recommendation: This regimen continues while responding until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Progression requires consultant reassessment; do not automatically continue the current pathway.

Withhold oral vinorelbine until counts recover and oncology/pharmacy reconcile the selected product, dose and protocol; do not issue an automatic 80% restart.

summary: Select IV or oral vinorelbine before issuing supportive medicines.
IV: minimal emetic risk; no routine prophylaxis.
Oral: moderate–high; prescribe oral 5-HT3 prophylaxis using NCCP V6 and local policy.
Counsel on constipation; laxatives may be required.
HER2 premedication is not routine; previous reactions require an individual plan.
supportive_care.mapping_basis: Select vinorelbine route and active phase: IV minimal, oral moderate–high, HER2-only minimal. Use the dedicated route-specific selector.
